newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.6 pct in Dec - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.6 pct in Dec - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.6 percent in the first two weeks of fiscal December versus November, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 5.8 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 5.7 percent in the week ended December 14 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
"So far, people are telling us that business is on track," said Howard Eilenberg, retail analyst at Lynch, Jones & Ryan, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Apparel and accessories sold well during the survey period, while computers and durable home goods were sluggish.
"That is a concern," Eilenberg said. "The appliance business is not good."
Overall, retailers should see an improved 1996 holiday shopping season compared with 1995, although the picture is not yet clear, Eilenberg said.
"You really have to look at the combined November/December period when the dust settles," he said. Stores "will do better this year than a year ago."
